name: Line-fault dink game
summary: Live cross-court dink game to 11 with volleys allowed; each player tallies rallies they end with their own faults (foot in the zone, volley in the zone).
setup: Both players at the non-volley-zone line, cross-court, playing into one half of the court
Live dink rally; either player may volley a ball out of the air from behind the line; a speed-up is allowed only on a ball above net height
A foot on the line or in the zone during or right after a volley is an own fault (play it as your rules allow; the fault rules are UNVERIFIED in this app)
Game to 11 rallies; each player tallies rallies lost to their own faults; play 2 games
success_criterion: In a game to 11, lose at most 1 rally to your own faults
safety_notes: Speed-ups at close range: wear eye protection and aim speed-ups low, never at the face. Stop if in pain.
coach_rationale: (judgment) Line faults happen most when a player reaches for a volley under live pressure; a competitive dink game with volleys allowed produces exactly those moments and scores only own faults, the AN-07 fault share. Unverified coaching content until a human coach reviews the library (P15).
